text:
sophie: Heads-up — seeing intermittent Xid 61 + ECC corrected spikes on gpu-node-az3-021 during nightly batch runs. Before we RMA, I want to run a tighter repro/burn-in so we don't return a flaky node. Proposed: quarantine node, run combined memory + compute + PCIe stress for 48-72h, capture NVML/NVIDIA driver traces. Thoughts?

 tim: can you paste the kernel snippet you saw?

 sophie: here's the syslog tail (copied):
```
Mar 18 03:12:08 gpu-node-az3-021 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 61, PID=2847 0x0000000b
Mar 18 03:12:08 gpu-node-az3-021 kernel: NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00 has fallen off the bus.
Mar 18 03:12:08 gpu-node-az3-021 kernel: NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed for GPU 0000:65:00:00: -19
Mar 18 03:12:09 gpu-node-az3-021 kernel: EDAC MC0: ECC errors: CE count increased to 12
```
Not huge frequency but repeats across 3 nights. ECC corrected spikes line up with Xid events.

 ryan: agree quarantine. Add these to repro:
- continuous `cudaMemcpy` heavy pattern + kernel launches (compute)
- memory sweep to exercise ECC correction (allocate large buffers)
- PCIe interleaved load (flapping pcie-reset)
- cold power cycle every 12 hours (power-cycling catches thermal related flakes)
Example stress script:
```bash
# run for 72h
stress-ng --gpu 4 --gpu-method all --timeout 72h &
python3 ~/tools/gpu_mem_sweep.py --size 24G --iter 0 --loop &
# run nvml traces
/usr/local/bin/nvml_trace --out /var/log/nvml/gpu-node-az3-021.trace &
```

 infra-bot: node gpu-node-az3-021 tagged quarantine-2026-03-18 by @sophie :warning:

 maria: I'll add an automated drain + eviction job so k8s pods shift off before the hardware test. drain cmd: `kubectl drain gpu-node-az3-021 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` then `kubectl cordon`. I can land the pipeline today.

 oncall-ops: cost angle — if we run a 72h burn on a dedicated spare, we lose capacity. We should try west-2 spare pool first; if not available schedule it in next maintenance window (low traffic). Estimated lost capacity cost ~ $250/day.

 tim: for monitoring, here's a quick PromQL to watch ECC corrected and Xid-like kernel events (from node-exporter + driver exporter):
```
sum(rate(nvidia_gpu_ecc_errors_corrected_total{job="node-exporter"}[5m])) by (instance)
sum(rate(node_kernel_dmesg_messages_total{level="err", message=~".*Xid.*"}[5m])) by (instance)
```
Set an alert if ECC errors > 5/5m or Xid lines > 0/5m for a node under test.

 sophie: proposed final checklist (agreed by me/ryan/maria):
1) cordon & drain node (maria pipeline)
2) snapshot logs & nvml trace start: `nvml_trace --start`
3) run combined stress (72h preferred, minimum 48h) including: compute kernel storm, mem sweep, PCIe exercise, MIG toggle cycles
4) scheduled cold power cycle at 0h, 12h, 24h, 48h (automated via BMC IPMI)
5) collect `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,POWER,PCI`, `/var/log/nvml/*.trace`, and `nvidia-bug-report.sh` at end
6) if Xid 61 or uncorrectable errors reappear -> open vendor escalation ticket + hold node from re-entering pool
7) if no repro after 72h -> do a 1-week staggered test: re-enable in canary pool with continuous monitoring and lower weight

 tim: minor add — capture GPU temperature + power telemetry every 30s (prom push + local csv) so we can correlate thermal spikes.

 ryan: also run a `lspci -vvv` before/after to catch PCI link width downgrades. If link width drops intermittently that's a hardware/slot issue.

 sophie: ok let's do 72h run on node gpu-node-az3-021 starting in 30min. maria, can you kick the drain/cordon pipeline? oncall-ops please reserve west-2 spare pool fallback. I'll post results in a follow-up thread and attach traces.

 maria: starting pipeline now. will post k8s evict logs here.

 infra-bot: pipeline `drain-quarantine` started for gpu-node-az3-021 by maria.

 oncall-ops: west-2 spare pool reserved (fallback) — tagging ticket INFRA-3427.

 sophie: thanks everyone. If we see repeat Xid events during the run we escalate immediately. If not, we move to staggered canary re-enable. :white_check_mark:
